did.unittitle: Brooklyn, New York, N.Y. Lewis Avenue Congregational Church records, 1888-1951.
did.abstract: The Grace Congregational Church in Brooklyn, New York, New York, was gathered on December 22, 1877. In 1880, the name was changed to Lewis Avenue Congregational Church. Land for the church was purchased in 1889 and a permanent edifice was completed in 1894. In 1944, the church building was sold to the Cornerstone Baptist Church. The church remained active until 1951 when it was formally dissolved. This collection contains administrative and membership records including meeting minutes, financial records, baptismal records, and correspondence.

custodhist.head: Custodial History
custodhist.p: Materials in this collection, except the correspondence folder, were given to the New York Conference of the United Church of Christ at an unknown time, likely following the church's dissolution. This collection was originally processed as part of the New York Conference records (RG0112) circa 1980.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: The Grace Congregational Church in Brooklyn, New York, New York, was gathered on December 22, 1877. Rev. James L. Hall was the first minister of the church. The name of the church was changed to Lewis Avenue Congregational Church in April, 1880. The church rented space formerly occupied by a Presbyterian congregation at the corner of Lewis Avenue and Monroe Street. In 1888, money was raised to purchase land for the church and in 1889, a lot on a different corner of Lewis Avenue and Monroe Street was purchased. The first service held in the new chapel was in November, 1889. In 1893, the cornerstone for an expanded church edifice was laid and the building was completed by May, 1894. The church's mortgage was paid off in 1908.

In 1944, the congregation sold the church building to the Cornerstone Baptist Church, an historically black congregation which had outgrown its previous location at Gates Avenue and Irving Place. Three quarters of the proceeds from the sale of the church went to the City Association to support its church extension work and the rest remained with the much-diminished Lewis Avenue Congregational Church. The church retained the Miles Memorial, a parish house adjacent to the church building, though it might have also been sold not long after the sale of the church building. The Lewis Avenue Congregational Church existed in some manner until 1951 when the church formally dissolved.
The Cornerstone Baptist Church remains active today in the same church building. In 2020, the Lewis Avenue Congregational Church was added to National Register of Historic Places.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This collection contains administrative and membership records for the Lewis Avenue Congregational Church in Brooklyn, New York, New York. The collection includes meeting minutes, annual reports, committee and trustee records, financial records, baptismal records, and some correspondence.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Materials in this collection have been arranged into chronological order by start date.
